subject: English
topic: Reported Speech II — Direct to Indirect (W11 B2)

questions.stem:
Change to indirect speech:
Direct: She said, "I am feeling unwell today."

options.option_text: She said that she is feeling unwell today.
She said that she was feeling unwell that day.
She said that I am feeling unwell today.
She said that she had been feeling unwell that day.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rules applied: (1) Pronoun: 'I' → 'she' (matches subject). (2) Tense backshift: 'am feeling' (present continuous) → 'was feeling' (past continuous). (3) Time word: 'today' → 'that day'. Result: 'She said that she was feeling unwell that day.' Trap: A keeps 'today' and present tense (no backshift); C keeps 'I' (pronoun not changed); D uses past perfect continuous (overcorrects — simple shift suffices).

questions.stem:
Change to indirect speech:
Direct: He said to me, "Have you finished your homework?"

options.option_text: He told me that I had finished my homework.
He asked me if I had finished my homework.
He asked me whether he had finished his homework.
He asked me if I finished my homework.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Question transformation rules: (1) Reporting verb: 'said to' → 'asked' (for questions). (2) Connector: Add 'if/whether' for Yes/No questions. (3) Pronoun: 'you' (addressee=me) → 'I'; 'your' → 'my'. (4) Tense: 'have finished' (present perfect) → 'had finished' (past perfect). Result: 'He asked me if I had finished my homework.' Trap: A uses 'told' (not for questions); C changes pronoun to 'he' (wrong — 'you' addressed to 'me' becomes 'I'); D keeps present perfect instead of past perfect.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct indirect speech:
Direct: The teacher said, "The Earth revolves around the Sun."

options.option_text: The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
The teacher told that Earth revolves around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth had revolved around the Sun.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Key rule: UNIVERSAL TRUTHS and SCIENTIFIC FACTS do not undergo tense change in indirect speech. 'The Earth revolves around the Sun' is a permanent scientific fact — the present tense 'revolves' is retained. Result: 'The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.' Trap: A uses 'revolved' (past tense — wrong for a scientific fact); B uses 'told' (wrong — 'tell' requires a person object: 'told him that...'; 'said that' is correct here); D uses past perfect (gross over-correction).

questions.stem:
Change to indirect speech:
Direct: He said to her, "Please open the window."

options.option_text: He told her to open the window.
He said to her to please open the window.
He told her that she should open the window.
He requested to her to open the window.

questions.explanation: A is correct. For polite requests/orders: reporting verb = 'told' (for commands) or 'requested' (for polite). The direct form 'Please + V' → indirect: 'told/requested + object + to + V'. Here: 'He told her to open the window.' The word 'please' is dropped in indirect speech (it's absorbed into 'requested' or 'told politely'). Trap: B keeps 'please' in indirect speech (not standard); C adds 'that she should' (overly complex for a simple command); D uses 'requested to her' (wrong — 'requested' takes a direct object without 'to': 'requested her to open').

questions.stem:
Change to indirect speech:
Direct: She said, "I will call you tomorrow."

options.option_text: She said that she would call me the next day.
She said that she will call you tomorrow.
She said that I will call you the following day.
She told that she would call me tomorrow.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Changes: (1) Pronoun: 'I' → 'she'; 'you' → 'me' (speaker addresses me). (2) Tense: 'will' → 'would'. (3) Time word: 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'. Result: 'She said that she would call me the next day.' Trap: B keeps 'will' and 'tomorrow' (no backshift); C keeps 'I' and 'you' (pronouns not changed); D uses 'told that' (wrong — 'tell' requires a person object).

questions.stem:
Change to indirect speech:
Direct: Ram said, "I was reading when she called."

options.option_text: Ram said that he was reading when she had called.
Ram said that he had been reading when she called.
Ram said that he was reading when she called.
Ram told that he had been reading when she had called.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Tense changes: 'was reading' (past continuous) → 'had been reading' (past perfect continuous). The verb 'called' (past simple) → 'called' (past simple, no change needed — time clauses in past do not always backshift further, and 'called' remains past simple to maintain the temporal relationship). Result: 'Ram said that he had been reading when she called.' Trap: A shifts 'called' to 'had called' (over-shifts the subordinate time clause — not standard); C makes no tense change in main verb; D uses 'told that' (wrong grammar — tell needs object).

questions.stem:
Change to indirect speech:
Direct: The doctor said to the patient, "Don't eat oily food."

options.option_text: The doctor said to the patient not to eat oily food.
The doctor told the patient that don't eat oily food.
The doctor advised the patient not to eat oily food.
The doctor asked the patient to not eat oily food.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Negative commands/instructions from a doctor: reporting verb = 'advised'. Negative imperative 'Don't + V' → 'advised + object + not to + V'. Result: 'The doctor advised the patient not to eat oily food.' Trap: A uses 'said to ... not to' (awkward — 'said to' is not used for reported commands); B keeps 'don't' in indirect speech (wrong); D uses 'asked ... to not' (the standard order is 'not to' not 'to not').

questions.stem:
Change to indirect speech:
Direct: He said, "What a beautiful painting this is!"

options.option_text: He said that it was a beautiful painting.
He exclaimed that what a beautiful painting it was.
He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful painting.
He said what a beautiful painting that was.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Exclamations (What a... / How...): reporting verb = 'exclaimed'. The exclamatory structure is dropped and replaced with 'that + declarative sentence'. 'What a beautiful painting' → 'it was a very beautiful painting' (add 'very' to express emphasis). Tense: 'is' → 'was'. Pronoun: 'this' → 'it'. Result: 'He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful painting.' Trap: A uses 'said' (wrong for exclamations); B keeps 'what a' (exclamatory structure retained — not standard indirect speech); D uses 'said' and keeps the exclamatory order.

questions.stem:
Change to indirect speech:
Direct: She said to him, "Where do you live?"

options.option_text: She asked him where did he live.
She asked him where he lived.
She told him where he lived.
She asked him that where does he live.

questions.explanation: B is correct. For Wh-questions in indirect speech: (1) Reporting verb: 'said to' → 'asked'. (2) No 'if/whether' — use the wh-word ('where') directly. (3) Word order: question order → statement order (do you live → he lived). (4) Tense: 'do live' → 'lived'. Result: 'She asked him where he lived.' Trap: A keeps question word order 'where did he live' (wrong — indirect speech uses statement word order without auxiliary 'did'); C uses 'told' (not for questions); D adds 'that' after wh-word (wrong — no 'that' needed after wh-words).

questions.stem:
Identify the correctly converted indirect speech:
Direct: He said, "I have never been to Paris."

options.option_text: He said that he had never been to Paris.
He said that he has never been to Paris.
He said that he never went to Paris.
He told he had never been to Paris.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Tense: 'have been' (present perfect) → 'had been' (past perfect). Pronoun: 'I' → 'he'. Paris is a proper noun — no change. Result: 'He said that he had never been to Paris.' Trap: B keeps 'has been' (no tense change — wrong); C changes 'have never been' to 'never went' (wrong tense transformation — present perfect does not become simple past); D uses 'told' without an object (wrong — 'told' must be followed by a person: 'told him that').
